title: Dynamics 365 Contact Center: route returning customers to a previous or preferred expert
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, routing behavior, administrator controls and publication-based credit consumption are supported. The stated gaps are appropriately narrow; documented record operations do not establish an API procedure for publishing a playbook.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched", "statusKey": "launched"

claims.claim: The roadmap target is October CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "October CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is June CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "June CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope

claims.claim: Unified routing can assign a returning customer's conversation to an expert who previously engaged with that customer.
claims.quote: This scenario assigns conversations to an expert who previously interacted with the customer within a configured time window.

claims.claim: The playbook can instead assign a conversation to a preferred expert mapped to the contact.
claims.quote: When a conversation enters the queue, the system checks for a preferred expert mapped to the contact.

claims.claim: Administrators define assignment logic using natural-language conversation orchestration playbooks.
claims.quote: Administrators define assignment logic by using natural language playbooks through conversation orchestration.

claims.claim: The Assign to a previous or preferred expert playbook lets administrators configure precedence between preferred and previous experts.
claims.quote: Admins can change the priority between preferred and previous experts to fit their business needs.

claims.claim: Administrators can configure the look-back period in the Assign to a previous or preferred expert playbook.
claims.quote: You can configure the precedence order and the look back period with conditions based on context variables by using the **Assign to a previous or preferred expert** playbook in conversation orchestration.

claims.claim: The default priority order is preferred expert, previous expert, then fallback.
claims.quote:
| 1 | Preferred Expert | Relationship manager or service representative mapped to the contact |
| 2 | Previous Expert | Expert who handled prior interaction within recency window |
| 3 | Fallback | Next best available expert using queue's assignment method |

claims.claim: Before assignment, an expert must have an allowed presence status.
claims.quote: | Presence check | Expert must be in an allowed presence status |

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The selected expert must belong to the relevant queue.
claims.quote: | Queue membership | Expert must be a member of the relevant queue |

claims.claim: A previous interaction must fall within the configured recency window.
claims.quote: Previous interaction must be within configured time period such as 7, 10, or 30 days.

claims.claim: Learn gives 7, 10 and 30 days as recency-window examples.
claims.quote: Previous interaction must be within configured time period such as 7, 10, or 30 days.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The recency-window cut-off supports up to 30 days.
claims.quote: The system supports up to 30 days cut off period for the recency window.

claims.claim: If neither preferred nor previous experts qualify, fallback invokes the queue's configured assignment method.
claims.quote:
1. Detects that no preferred or previous expert is available or eligible.
2. Invokes the queue's configured assignment method.
3. Assigns the conversation to the next best available expert.

claims.claim: Using preferred-expert assignment through playbooks requires preferred representatives to be configured.
claims.quote: You must configure preferred representatives if you want to configure assignment to a preferred expert by using playbooks through conversation orchestration.

claims.claim: Keep the same expert for async chats reconnects returning chats when the previous representative meets configured presence and active-conversation-limit checks.
claims.quote: For returning asynchronous chats, keeps the same expert when representative affinity is enabled and the expert meets the presence and active conversation limit requirements.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout; controls[1].note
claims.claim: Administrators can configure async fallback to the next best representative or leave the chat unassigned in the queue.
claims.quote:
Select one of the following **fallback**options if the previous expert isn't available:
    - **assign to next best expert in queue**
    - **keep the chat unassigned in the queue**

claims.claim: The async playbook applies to queues where representative affinity is enabled.
claims.quote: Configure this behavior for queues where representative affinity is enabled by using the **Keep the same expert for async chats** playbook in conversation orchestration.

claims.claim: Conversation orchestration is available for voice and messaging channels only.
claims.quote: Conversation orchestration is available for voice and messaging channels only.

claims.where: summary; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost; front matter: cost
claims.claim: Publishing a conversation orchestration playbook consumes Copilot credits, supporting the variable cost rating.
claims.quote: Conversation orchestration consumes Copilot credits only when you publish a playbook, which makes the configured orchestration logic active for use.

claims.claim: A published playbook can process any number of customer conversations without extra Copilot credits.
claims.quote: After you publish, the playbook can process any number of customer conversations without consuming extra Copilot credits.

claims.claim: Saving a playbook as a draft does not consume Copilot credits.
claims.quote: When you save the playbook as a draft or enable conversation orchestration, it doesn't consume Copilot credits.

claims.claim: Enabling conversation orchestration does not consume Copilot credits.
claims.quote: When you save the playbook as a draft or enable conversation orchestration, it doesn't consume Copilot credits.

claims.quote: Specific licensing requirements apply to configure and use conversation orchestration in Dynamics 365 Contact Center. Learn more in Dynamics 365 Licensing Guide.

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed, combining Dynamics 365 licensing requirements with consumption-based billing.
claims.quote: Specific licensing requirements apply to configure and use conversation orchestration in Dynamics 365 Contact Center. ... Set up consumption-based billing.

claims.claim: The cited Learn prerequisites do not name a specific licence for conversation orchestration and instead refer readers to the licensing guide.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: Consumption-based billing must be set up for conversation orchestration.
claims.quote: Set up consumption-based billing.

claims.quote: Dynamics 365 supports two billing models: prepaid capacity and pay-as-you-go.

claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go requires an Azure subscription.
claims.quote: To set up pay-as-you-go billing, you first need an active Azure subscription.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A Copilot credit rate per published playbook for this scenario is not yet published.

claims.claim: Editing an active playbook uses Save & publish.
claims.quote: **For active playbooks**: Select **Save & publish** to save and immediately publish your changes.

claims.claim: Previous-expert assignment retrieves previous experts from the customer's interaction history.
claims.quote: Retrieves the previous experts from the customer's interaction history.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The cited feature pages do not describe a separate retention setting for the history used to find previous experts.
claims.quote: Searched: "previous expert" "retention" Dynamics 365; conversation orchestration previous expert interaction history retention setting enable feature toggle. Read configure-preferred-agent and configure-conversation-orchestration; no separate history-retention setting stated.

claims.claim: Preferred representatives can be mapped to contacts only in the documented configuration experience.
claims.quote: You can map representatives to contacts only.

claims.claim: Up to three preferred representatives can be mapped to a contact.
claims.quote: You can map up to three preferred representatives to a contact.

claims.claim: Finding a preferred representative requires the incoming customer's contact to be identified.
claims.quote: To find the preferred representative for an incoming work item, the contact should be identified.

claims.claim: A published playbook automatically assigns conversations rather than requiring supervisor approval for each assignment.
claims.quote: Conversation orchestration monitors each conversation as conditions evolve ... and automatically runs the relevant action in accordance with your configured playbooks.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Publishing converts natural-language playbooks into a structured runtime format using a language model.
claims.quote: When you publish a playbook, the system uses a language model to convert it into a structured runtime format that the system then uses to perform playbook actions.

claims.claim: The converted output might not fully capture the intended playbook logic.
claims.quote: Because the system uses a language model to convert natural language playbooks into a structured runtime format, the converted output might not fully capture the intended logic.

claims.claim: Deviations between intended and converted logic can be identified only during runtime.
claims.quote: You can identify any deviations only during runtime.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft advises testing and monitoring runtime behavior and revising playbooks when orchestration does not work as intended.
claims.quote: Administrators should test and monitor runtime behavior and revise the playbook if orchestration doesn't work as intended.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A returning async conversation can reconnect below the active conversation limit even when that limit exceeds the configured capacity profile.
claims.quote: If the total is below the limit, the system reconnects the conversation to the same representative, even when the limit exceeds the configured capacity profile.

claims.claim: Microsoft says the feature should not be used for decisions affecting employment, compensation or similar employee rights.
claims.quote: This feature isn't intended for use in making—and shouldn't be used to make—decisions that affect the employment of an employee or group of employees, including compensation, rewards, seniority, or other rights or entitlements.

claims.quote: Verify the queue membership and presence status of the previous representatives and check if their last interactions with the customer was within the configured recency window.

claims.claim: Conversation orchestration diagnostics can be read using a custom query.
claims.quote: You can view the diagnostics information by using a custom query.

claims.quote: **Support English only**: The system currently supports the English language only.

claims.quote: **All queues**: Applies to all queues for the selected channel. ... **List of queues**: Select specific queues from the list. ... **All queues except**: Applies to all queues except the ones you exclude.
